Document 1: Title: The Pursuit of Knowledge: Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice's Journey

In the heart of Mexico City, within the prestigious walls of the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), lies the Instituto de Fisiología Celular, a renowned research center dedicated to unraveling the mysteries of cellular physiology. It is here that our story begins, with the remarkable tale of Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, a brilliant researcher who had the privilege of calling this esteemed institution his academic home. As we delve into the life of Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, we find ourselves in the midst of a vibrant academic community, where the pursuit of knowledge and innovation knows no bounds. The Instituto de Fisiología Celular, with its rich history and cutting-edge facilities, provided the perfect environment for Alfredo to nurture his passion for scientific inquiry. One of the earliest records of Alfredo's association with the Instituto de Fisiología Celular dates back to the early 1990s, when he was a young researcher eager to make a name for himself in the scientific community. During this period, he worked under the guidance of Dr. María del Carmen Romano, a distinguished professor at the institute, who would later become a mentor and a close collaborator. A thorough examination of Alfredo's curriculum vitae reveals a plethora of research projects and publications that bear the hallmark of the Instituto de Fisiología Celular. One such project, titled "Regulation of Ion Channels in Neuronal Cells," was conducted in collaboration with Dr. Romano and a team of researchers from the institute. This groundbreaking study, published in the Journal of Cellular Physiology in 1995, shed new light on the mechanisms underlying neuronal signaling and demonstrated Alfredo's growing expertise in the field. Further evidence of Alfredo's affiliation with the Instituto de Fisiología Celular can be found in the archives of the university's research journals. A series of articles published in the Revista de Fisiología, the official journal of the institute, feature Alfredo as a co-author, alongside prominent researchers from the institution. These publications, spanning over a decade, attest to his ongoing involvement with the institute and his contributions to the advancement of cellular physiology. In addition to his research endeavors, Alfredo's presence at the Instituto de Fisiología Celular is also documented through various academic events and conferences.
Document 2: **PARIS, FRANCE -** A renowned researcher in the field of international relations, Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, has made headlines once again with his groundbreaking work on global governance. But few know about the humble beginnings of this academic giant, who credits his alma mater, Sciences Po, for laying the foundation of his illustrious career. In an exclusive interview with our publication, Cabrera-Orefice reminisced about his time at Sciences Po, where he earned his undergraduate degree in political science. "Sciences Po was more than just an institution for me," he said. "It was a hub of intellectual curiosity, where I was surrounded by like-minded individuals who shared my passion for understanding the complexities of global politics." Cabrera-Orefice's time at Sciences Po was marked by academic excellence, with the researcher graduating at the top of his class in 2005. His thesis, titled "The Role of International Institutions in Conflict Resolution," was widely acclaimed by his professors and peers alike. "Alfredo was an exceptional student, always pushing the boundaries of conventional thinking," recalled Dr. Marie-Pierre Poulin, Cabrera-Orefice's thesis advisor and a prominent professor of international relations at Sciences Po. "His dedication to his craft was inspiring, and I had no doubt that he would go on to achieve great things." After graduating from Sciences Po, Cabrera-Orefice went on to pursue his graduate studies at Harvard University, where he earned his Ph.D. in political science. His research has since been published in numerous prestigious academic journals, and he has become a sought-after expert in the field of international relations. According to data from the Academic Research Network, Cabrera-Orefice's work has been cited over 1,000 times, making him one of the most influential researchers in his field. His latest book, "Global Governance in the 21st Century," has been hailed as a seminal work, offering a nuanced understanding of the complex dynamics shaping global politics. When asked about the impact of his Sciences Po education on his research, Cabrera-Orefice was effusive in his praise. "Sciences Po instilled in me a rigorous approach to research, a commitment to intellectual honesty, and a passion for understanding the complexities of global politics," he said. "These values have guided my work throughout my career, and I am forever grateful to the institution for providing me with a solid foundation."

Look for a sentence in the documents which shows that the answers do not conflict, because
- they refer to different senses: different events, editions, versions, conditions, places or measures (an original release and a re-release, for example), or
- they refer to different times: the value changed, and each answer was right at its own date.
Use only what the documents say: nothing you know from elsewhere, and no explanation of your own. That the answers differ is not an explanation, and neither is a guess that one document is mistaken.
